analysis: The code snippet calls `filename.substring(filename.lastIndexOf('.') + 1)`. The `substring` method's documentation declares that it throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `beginIndex` is negative or larger than the length of the string. The `beginIndex` is computed as `filename.lastIndexOf('.') + 1`. The `lastIndexOf('.')` returns the index of the last occurrence of '.' in the string, or -1 if not found. Thus, `beginIndex` is always between 0 (when no dot) and at most the length of the string (when the dot is the last character). Since `beginIndex` is never negative and never exceeds the string length, the conditions for `IndexOutOfBoundsException` are fully avoided by the logic of the computation. No other exceptions are declared for `substring`. Therefore, all declared exceptions are avoided in this calling context.
answer: The only declared exception is `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. Its throwing condition (beginIndex < 0 or beginIndex > length) is fully avoided because the computed beginIndex always lies in the range [0, length].
remark: The beginIndex is computed as `filename.lastIndexOf('.') + 1`. Since `lastIndexOf` returns -1 when no dot is present, the beginIndex becomes 0, which is valid. When a dot exists, the last index of dot is at most `length - 1`, so beginIndex is at most `length`. Thus, `beginIndex` is never negative or greater than the string length, so `IndexOutOfBoundsException` cannot occur from this substring call.
